summary: Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and served as chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Goldman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1952–1955) and held a post at Wayne State University (~1956–1989).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He later held posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian and archaeologist. He held academic posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1987–1992) and at Heidelberg University (~2003).

Bernfried Schlerath was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics scholar who studied under Paul Thieme (~1953–1956). He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1964–1969), University of Marburg (~1969–1974), and Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist who served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1935–1945), where he succeeded Heinrich Lüders.

Bernhard Forssman specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1958–1964) under Karl Hoffmann (~1960–1964), and later held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn across several universities, later holding posts at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian and Tibetan-Iranian Institutes (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp, completing studies in Zurich, Berlin, Göttingen, and Paris. He held several academic posts at the University of Zurich as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar in sinology and linguistics who studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915). He later held academic posts at Uppsala University (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Frankfurt and Cologne, among other universities. He held posts at the University of Cologne (1966–1970, 1972–1976), Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied at NYU, Brooklyn Polytechnic, and UCLA, and trained under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He co-founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and founded Zen Peacemakers in 1980.

Bert Vaux is a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago (1986–1990) and Harvard University (1990–1994). He held academic posts at Harvard (1994–2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003–2006), and the University of Cambridge (2006–2010).

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and Oxford, completing her doctorate under Jonathan A. Silk in 2010. She held posts at Heidelberg University (~2015–2016) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, and Franz Bopp in Halle and Berlin. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1867–1870) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, completing his PhD at Leipzig under August Conrady. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History (1901, 1904–1906), Columbia University (1905–1907), and the Field Museum (1907).

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied in Munich, Vienna, and other universities, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at BHU, the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge is a sinologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama. She was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Georg Simmel, Emil Sieg, and Eugen Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Hamburg (1931–1933), the University of London (~1934–1945), and the University of Colombo (1945–1949).
